R387.note: Removes Process.Start entirely and probes with System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping, so serverName is never re-parsed as PowerShell; the output format differs from Test-Connection's and an empty serverName now returns 400, both stated and neither blocks a legitimate caller.

R388.note: Stored extension now comes from file-type's detected.ext instead of req.file.originalname, which is exactly the sink's defect; response shape unchanged.

R389.note: Rejecting CR/LF in replyTo, recipient and subject at the hand-rolled SMTP sink closes the command-injection vector without stripping; the added null rejection only affects a value that was never a valid address.

R390.note: Parameterized query via @actor with AddWithValue; contract preserved, apostrophes are now literal data.

R391.note: Random hex name plus detected.ext removes the client filename from the path and the served extension; JSON url and 400 error shape preserved (SVG remaining allowed is pre-existing, not introduced).

R392.note: app.UseAntiforgery() alone validates only endpoints carrying IAntiforgeryMetadata, which minimal APIs add automatically only for form-bound parameters; this JSON-bound endpoint gets no RequireAntiforgery() metadata, so the middleware skips it and the write-up's claim that all POSTs are now validated is wrong - nothing else observable changes.

R393.note: Magic-byte check on the declared type before Files.copy closes content spoofing; MultipartFile.getInputStream() returns a fresh stream per call so the second read is intact, though the first header stream is never closed (minor leak, not observable to callers).

R394.note: Secure: true closes the finding; HttpOnly is extra hardening, stated, and blocks no legitimate use.

R395.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding().withRootObject(order) keeps property arithmetic over the record and rejects T(), constructors, method calls and bean refs, matching the stated contract.

R396.note: Moving the session write below login_user() is a no-op in Flask's signed-cookie session - the same dict is serialized once at response time - and the fix neither clears/rotates the pre-login session nor checks login_user()'s return value, so nothing about the weakness changes; nothing else changes either.

R397.note: json_decode closes the gadget-chain vector, but every existing cookie was written with serialize() (the original's instanceof check requires that), so json_decode returns null and every legitimate cart silently restores empty; the write-up claims functionality is preserved and never says the cookie writer must change - the format-preserving fix was unserialize(..., ['allowed_classes' => ['ShoppingCart']]).

R398.note: Bound positional parameter with the wildcards kept in code; LIKE '%...%' substring semantics preserved exactly as the contract requires.

R399.note: Build FAIL (CS0120: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(byte[]) is not static on this target), so the fix does not compile; the design (CSPRNG, seed ignored) is otherwise sound and the ignored seed is stated.

R400.note: Explicit noent/dtdload/dtdvalid false on parseXml is the correct libxmljs mechanism and leaves the XPath extraction unchanged; judged by reading since the binding could not load.

R401.note: Server-chosen random name with an extension from a fixed image allowlist removes the client filename from the path and stops non-image extensions landing under static/; the allowlist and random path are both stated and only reject uploads whose name has no image extension.

R402.note: Gate::authorize() enforces the check by throwing AuthorizationException (403); authorized callers proceed unchanged.

R403.note: getHost()==null admits opaque URIs: verified in a scratch dir that new URI("http:evil.com").getHost() is null while browsers resolve it to host evil.com, so an external redirect still passes; the check also rejects same-host absolute URLs the original accepted, a stated restriction beyond the vector.
